podcast.title: Contribution to Al Purdy Tribute
podcast.body: Sarah Harmer was one of the artists who contributed to the soundtrack of the 2015 documentary on Al Purdy, which featured songs and poems inspired by the poet. "Bruce Cobra and Greg Kieler of Blue Rodeo, Sarah Harmer, Jason Collette of Broken Social Scene, even Margaret Atwood appeared on that album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ian Thorneley's Session Work
xref.body: Ian Thorneley worked as a session player for Nickelback, among other artists, after the initial breakup of Big Wreck. "If you look in the line of notes for albums by Nickelback and Sarah Harmer and Stephen Fearing, you'll see his name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ian Thornley - In His Own Words: Part 2

xref.title: Post-Big Wreck Version 1.0 Career Transition
xref.body: After Big Wreck's initial disbandment around 2001-2002, Ian Thorneley moved back to Toronto and found work as a session player. He contributed to albums by artists such as Nickelback, Sarah Harmer, and Stephen Fearing. "After big rec version 1.0 broke up, Ian moved back to Toronto where he found work as a session player."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Bathhouse Recording Studio
xref.body: The Tragically Hip owns and operates its own recording studio, known as The Bathhouse, located outside of Kingston. This studio has served as a recording location for numerous other artists, including Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blackie and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, The Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, The Trews, and The Mahones. "The hip has their own recording studio outside of Kingston called the Bathhouse. Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blacky and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, the Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, the Trues, the Mahones and dozens of others have used the place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
